findings.title: canManage() grants group management to holders of only the VIEW scope
findings.body: In V2, canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because the scope list includes VIEW, any admin with a view-only permission on the Groups type passes canManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage(), so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. The management check should only accept MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) already does.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource UUIDs and looks groups up by the wrong key
findings.body: In V2 each group's Resource is created with name = group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource uses resolveGroup's group id as the name). Lines 121-123 instead add groupResource.getId(), which is the internal resource UUID, not the group id. Line 122 also passes that resource UUID into hasPermission, which calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so the per-group lookup misses and the code falls back to the all-groups resource. The result is a set of meaningless IDs. Callers use it as a group-ID filter (UserModel.GROUPS and getUsersCount), so users reachable only via a group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission are never listed or counted. The fix is to use groupResource.getName() for both the lookup and the collected ID.

findings.title: NullPointerException when the Groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission, when the per-group resource is missing, the code loads the all-groups type resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource is absent (e.g. a realm whose schema resources were never initialised), so this throws an NPE instead of returning false. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same pattern for the Users type.

findings.title: Impersonation context uses the target user as the evaluated identity
findings.body: When a requester is given, canImpersonate builds a DefaultEvaluationContext with new UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the identity being impersonated, not the admin performing the action. Policies attached to the IMPERSONATE permission are then evaluated against the target user's identity. When requester is null, the context is null and evaluation uses the admin's identity. The two paths therefore evaluate different principals, so a policy such as 'only my admin' can allow or deny impersonation depending on whether a client id was passed.

findings.title: Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission describes the wrong return type
findings.body: The @return tag says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method returns a Set<String>. The sentence before it also reads 'returns empty set', which is correct, but the two statements together are inconsistent with the signature.

findings.title: Public helper searchGroupModelsByAttributes removed from a server SPI module
findings.body: ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes was deleted. It is public in server-spi-private, so any downstream extension or provider code calling it will fail to compile. The only in-repo caller was updated, but the removal is an unannounced API break in a non-test module.

findings.title: getResourceName has no display name for Groups resources
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases USERS to show usernames and 'All users', but nothing handles GROUPS. Group permission resources therefore fall back to resource.getDisplayName(), which is typically the raw group UUID. The admin console will show opaque IDs for group permissions, unlike users and clients.

findings.title: Group membership test does not cover the negative case or the view-members path via listing
findings.body: testManageGroupMembership and testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers only assert the positive path. No test checks that a user in a group where the admin lacks VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS is hidden, and no test covers the all-groups Groups-type permission combined with a per-group view-members grant. Given the ID bug in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, the group-membership filter path is the one most likely to regress and is not exercised for V2 from the group-listing side.
